rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Setup 3 Turns (after setup) 4 Scoring Objective Standard: First to remove 3 rings wins. Blitz: First to form 1 row wins. Setup Each player gets 5 rings (black or white). Players alternate placing their rings on empty intersections. Turns (after setup) Place a marker of your color inside one of your rings. Move that ring in a straight line (any distance) to an empty space. If you jump over a series of markers (any color), the ring must land in the first empty space of that line. All jumped-over markers are flipped to the opposite color. You may not jump over other rings regardless of their color. Scoring If you create a row of 5 markers of your color: Remove those 5 markers from the board. Remove one of your rings from the board. If the pool of 51 markers runs out: The player with the most rings removed wins. If both players have removed the same number of rings, the game ends in a draw.

---

In YINSH, the players each start with five rings on the board. Every time a ring is moved, it leaves a marker behind. Markers are white on one side and black on the other. When markers are jumped over by a ring they must be flipped, so their color is constantly changing. The players must try to form a row of five markers with their own color face up. If a player succeeds in doing so, he removes one of his rings as an indication that he has formed such a row. The first player to remove three of his rings wins the game. In other words, each row you make brings you closer to victory-but also makes you weaker, because you have one fewer ring to play with. Very tricky!

[Rating: 2/10] Pretty clever GIPF game, jumping the pieces to flip their colors adds an interesting wrinkle to the movement and positioning of your rings plus the rubberbanding catchup mechanism of losing your pieces as you score keeps it a pretty close game for its short playtime. The setup and early game does feel a tad like both players are fumbling in the dark until threats become glaringly obvious though, of course experienced players will recognize the potentials of each move but it is a slight against the game for the casual level that I play it at, otherwise I quite enjoy this one.
